messages.content:
You write the two short notices Ryde sends after a dispute ruling: one to the rider, one to the driver.
Each ≤ 120 words, plain English, second person, no legalese: state the outcome, the one or two facts that decided it,
the amount and how it is paid (Ryde voucher), and what it means for the recipient (e.g. account review). Do not cite
ids like F3 or RD-2. If the case was escalated to a human reviewer, say only that and what the reviewer will look at —
do not state a conclusion and do not promise a timeframe (the routing notice carries the service level). Return JSON: {"rider": "...", "driver": "..."}

Case B-0026. Outcome: refund_full $6.61. Recommended action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and refer the driver's fake "I'm Here" arrival tap to Ryde account review + flag_account. Escalated: False.
Reasoning:
This is a driver-initiated no-show cancellation, so NS-0 routes the $6.61 fee to the NS-1/NS-2 test [F3][RD-2 not applicable][NS-0]. The trace settles the three limbs: (i) pass (a tap at 12:05:55) [F5], (ii) fail — 601 m at the tap, closest approach 545 m overall, never inside 200 m [F5][F1], (iii) fail — 0 s inside the radius after the tap [F5][F2]. Under NS-1 all of (i)(ii)(iii) must hold, so the fee cannot stand [F1][F3][NS-1].

The driver's statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] and the 12:06 chat "I'm here already" [F9] are contradicted by the GPS/timeline records: he stood stationary 3 min 30 s at 600 m from the pickup, not at it [F2][F5], and system records override statements [F1][F9][NS-1]. Duration alone (3 min 30 s) does not cure a wait served outside the pickup location [F2][F3][NS-1].

Accordingly NS-2 applies: the fee of $6.61, recorded on the fare [F7] for an unconsummated RydeX booking with no surge [F8], is refunded in full to the rider [F3][F7][NS-2]. Refund is issued as a Ryde voucher, no cash [F7][NS-7].

Independently, NS-2's account-review condition is met: a recorded "I'm Here" tap [F5] while GPS placed the driver 601 m outside the pickup range [F1] is the fake-arrival-tap trigger. The driver's otherwise clean record (0 disputes upheld in 502 trips) [F17] is a profile fact and cannot defeat the trigger [F5][F1][NS-2].

Amount = cancellation fee $6.61 as recorded on the fare [F3][F7][NS-2]. No separate detour or FARE arithmetic applies (no off-route segment facts in this file) [F3][NS-0].

function.name: final_result
function.description: The final response which ends this conversation

function.name: final_result
function.arguments: {"rider": "We reviewed your cancellation fee and you're getting it back in full: $6.61, issued as a Ryde voucher (no cash). What decided it: the driver cancelled as a no-show, but his arrival tap came from about 600 m away from the pickup point, and he was never within the pickup range at any point. Waiting time doesn't count when it isn't served at the pickup spot. No action is needed from you — the voucher will be applied to your account.", "driver": "Your no-show cancellation fee of $6.61 will not be charged to the rider and has been refunded to them as a Ryde voucher. The reason: your \"I'm Here\" tap was recorded about 600 m from the pickup point, and the location records show you never entered the pickup range. Sitting for 3 minutes 30 seconds doesn't count when it isn't at the pickup spot, and system records take priority over statements. Separately, the arrival tap is being referred to account review, which will look at the tap and your location data at that moment."}
